answer: A saffron ledger assigns each identity a unique willow key and requires a fresh beacon proof for every registration attempt. The enforcement rule rejects any identity whose proof cannot be verified as newly generated, so an attacker cannot precompute valid proofs before the registration window opens. Each identity must pay a per-registration fee that scales with the number of pending proof requests, making mass account creation expensive. The cost stays fixed per identity, so a single attacker cannot spread the expense across many accounts.
